title: Pinned real Ribasim BMI-driven management clock with daily output

sequencing.rationale: Freeze the coupler-clock hypothesis and numerical references before observing DUMMY-19G and DUMMY-19H.

source_binding.bmi_update_until: core/src/bmi.jl::BMI.update_until adds the requested endpoint to allocation.time.tstops before stepping.
source_binding.allocation_loop: core/src/model.jl::loopheader! solves allocation whenever current model time equals the first allocation tstop.
source_binding.consequence: Repeated coupler update_until calls can introduce allocation boundaries finer than solver.saveat; saveat remains a separate additional source of tstop boundaries.

purpose: Test whether the coupler can own a 6-hour management clock through BMI.update_until while solver output remains daily, and whether that reproduces the same physical and allocation trajectory as the analytically preregistered 6-hour clock case.
hypotheses: With solver.saveat=86400 s, BMI.update_until endpoints at 6-hour intervals introduce 6-hour allocation solves without 6-hour output.
The internal allocation sequence after each BMI call matches the preregistered 6-hour state-feedback allocation sequence.
The one-day physical recipient volumes and Basin endpoint match the DUMMY-19G 21600-second hybrid reference.
Both priority orders preserve identical total physical supply and Basin endpoint while differing in recipient delivery.
This establishes that a coupler can introduce an explicit management clock finer than output saveat in the pinned implementation.
It does not establish that saveat is neutral when saveat itself is finer than the coupler clock.
forbidden: no changing BMI call endpoints after execution
no post-output tuning to DUMMY-19G observations
no claim that BMI removes saveat-triggered allocation boundaries
